question: What is the minimum number of consecutive sub-epsilon or no-win rounds required to trigger a converge/stuck state in the optimize loop?
gold: OPTIMIZE_DEFAULTS spreads optimize.DEFAULTS = { epsilon: 0.01, diminishing_rounds: 3 }: epsilon is the per-cycle improvement below which a round counts as diminishing; K=3 consecutive sub-epsilon/no-win rounds trigger converge/stuck. A negative/NaN knob falls back to default (a mis-set knob must not silently disable the control). Budget reuses the loop's tokenBudget â€” no separate knob.
title: Optimize-loop convergence defaults: epsilon=0.01, diminishing_rounds=3

question: What is the minimum overlap score required to flag a candidate as a likely re-plan duplicate, and what two conditions must the matched task satisfy for the warning to trigger?
gold: SUGGEST_DUP_THRESHOLD=0.6: a candidate scoring >=0.6 label/summary overlap is flagged a likely re-plan duplicate, but ONLY when the matched task is in an OPEN status and kind !== 'note'. Notes and terminal tasks never trigger the dup warning.
title: suggest_links dup threshold 0.6 fires only on OPEN non-note tasks

question: What is the specific reason that graph-dependent and wincase-c are excluded from scoped regret despite the gate firing on them?
gold: graph-dependent and wincase-c retrieve the SAME note as the positive and are textually NEARER to it, so the recalibrated gate fires on them (2/2). They are NOT counted in scoped regret only because the note post-dates them (it could not have been retrieved at their run time). This proves a structural limit: a note<->task gate cannot detect held-out-ness â€” that property is environmental, external to the gate's inputs.
title: Same-micro-domain controls fire the gate but are excluded from regret on temporal grounds

question: What percentage of agent records in the registry lack a session and can only be recovered via time-window-overlap correlation against byWindow?
gold: The task-transcript / resolveOwner held-out win: the spec describes only direct + session resolution, but ~40% of this registry's agent records have no session and are recoverable ONLY by time-window-overlap correlation against byWindow. That fact lives in a pre-seeded note (originally note-mq7kyiir6sx); the OFF arm must derive the strategy from scratch and never references byWindow.
title: resolveOwner win rests on ~40% of registry records lacking a session, recoverable only via byWindow

question: What specific percentage figure represents the self-similar corpus's POI (point of interest) rate that may not transfer to customer projects?
gold: All benchmark numbers come from one operator running the orchestrator instrumenting its OWN memory system â€” maximally self-similar. What transfers to a customer project is the CATEGORY (every project accumulates its own local empirical facts), not the notes themselves and not necessarily the 23% point estimate.
title: Standing caveat: the corpus is maximally self-similar (orchestrator benchmarking itself)

question: What fraction of the "winnable" tasks fall into the "benchmark-meta" category versus the "transfer-robust general-infra" category according to Phase 0a's split?
gold: Phase 0a found 18/52 'winnable' (external-gap + empirical + load-bearing), splitting them 12 'benchmark-meta' (project-local measured verdicts) vs 6 'transfer-robust general-infra'. Phase 1 INVERTED Phase 0a's bet: the general-infra slice is exactly what pretraining covers (0/4 traps survived), while the project-local-meta slice is where both real wins live. Honest frequency = ~23% (12/52), not the general-infra slice Phase 0a guessed at ~10â€“15%.
title: Winnable regime is ~23% (12/52) of note-dependent tasks â€” the project-local-measured slice

question: What was the approximate hardness multiplier from the lowest-context arm (H_off) to the highest-context arm (dagrag) in the v4 measurement?
gold: First real semantic RAG (MiniLM) + DAG context, 4 arms x 2 tasks: NO win on all 6 ON cells, and the combined DAG+RAG arm was the worst. Hardness rose monotonically with amount injected (v4: H_off 14,584 -> search 16,274 -> lean 19,969 -> dagrag 29,027, ~2x). Solve rate stayed 100% everywhere â€” context only added deliberation. v7 also closed the retrieval-quality alibi: semantic retrieval demonstrably worked and changed nothing; the blocker was never recall.
title: v7: the combined DAG+RAG arm was the WORST; hardness grows monotone in context amount

question: What billing rate do prompt-cache reads incur under `claude -p`, and what effect does this have on cost across both arms of the comparison?
gold: The audited ~90% memory-product savings compare against replaying full conversation history every turn â€” a baseline nobody competent runs. Under claude -p, prompt-cache reads bill at ~0.1x input and climb monotonically within a session, so the harness gives memory-like cost behavior to BOTH arms for free. Against real baselines the savings evaporate; cost difference was purely cache_read on the injected payload, with output tokens (real work) unmoved.
title: Vendor '90% token savings' is strawman-relative; prompt caching already gives both arms memory-like cost

question: What is the minimum cosine similarity score required for the top retrieved note to pass the context-gate injection check in lib/context-gate.js?
gold: lib/context-gate.js INJECTs a retrieved note only if ALL hold: top1 cosine >= 0.50 (cosThreshold) AND the top note classifies as 'empirical' (requireEmpirical) AND (margin >= 0.08 OR externalGap >= 0.25) AND projectLocality >= 2 of 4 (localityThreshold). Anything else ABSTAINS. Conservative by construction so every miss is a false-negative (missed win), never a wasted inject.
title: Context-gate inject rule: ABSTAIN by default; the exact 5-threshold gate

question: What is the approximate external-gap value of the true positive that distinguishes it from topical near-ties in the 0.50â€“0.55 MiniLM cluster?
gold: The first real positive sat at top1=0.548 inside a tight 0.50-0.55 MiniLM topical cluster where neither a raw cosine cut nor a margin cut can separate the true scar from topical near-ties. The external-gap (fraction of the note's content tokens that recur in the task text) does: positive ~0.34 vs every topical negative <=0.17. Thresholds are provisional, calibrated on n=1, and fragile to note supersession (a replacement note can drift below the floor).
title: cosThreshold was lowered 0.55->0.50; external-gap, not cosine/margin, discriminates

question: What text markers qualify a note as "principle" type yet disqualify it from inject?
gold: classifyNoteType derives empirical|principle|neutral purely from text markers (overlay addNoteNode stores no type). An empirical signature wins even if principle words also appear, but pure-principle phrasing ('always/never/best practice/prefer/generally') is DISQUALIFIED from inject because the base model already knows principles. Consequence: phrasing a genuine scar as a principle silently makes it non-injectable.
title: Note TYPE is inferred from text by regex â€” notes carry no explicit type field

question: What are the four categories a note must hit at least two of to pass the projectLocality guard?
gold: A note must hit >=2 of {measured (%/ N/M ratio), errval (NaN/ERR_/quoted digit/exit code), ident (camelCase/snake_case/path/call), observed ('empirically/discovered/observed/measured')} or the gate ABSTAINS 'non-local' even when the fact IS project-local. A migration-schema note written as plain prose scored locality=1 and was rejected; adding a function name like parseTaskId() or 'discovered empirically' pushes it to 2 and clears the guard.
title: projectLocality guard needs >=2 of 4 categories â€” phrasing alone can sink a real note

question: What file path patterns are in the fixed allow-list that permits writes without a claim in the orch-gate?
gold: The pre-tool claim gate (hooks/orch-gate.js) allows writes without a claim only for a fixed list: .claude/projects/**/memory/, .claude settings/keybindings/launch.json, .mcp.json, CLAUDE.md, .claude/orchestrator/tasks/, .claude/tasks/, /scratch/, *.log and /logs/. It deliberately does NOT exempt /tmp (//private/tmp) or .claude/orchestrator/ source. It also FAILS OPEN: no session_id, daemon unreachable, or orch-off all -> allow.
title: orch-gate FAILS OPEN and exempts a fixed allow-list; /tmp and orch source are NOT exempt

question: What is the cosThreshold value shared by both lib/context-gate.js and lib/ask-gate.js?
gold: lib/context-gate.js (inject-vs-abstain) and lib/ask-gate.js (predict-vs-ask) share the SAME four-guard shape and calibrated DEFAULTS: cosThreshold 0.50, gapThreshold 0.25 (external-gap), marginThreshold 0.08, localityThreshold 2 (of 4 project-locality categories), requireEmpirical true. Both default to the safe action (abstain / ask) and only fire on a high-confidence, specific, project-local, empirical note match. Change one set of thresholds and you almost certainly want to change the other.
title: context-gate and ask-gate are twin abstain/ask-by-default gates with identical shipped thresholds

question: What is the cosine floor value that the discriminator was lowered to, and why does neither raw cosine nor top1-top2 margin cut work as a separator for MiniLM's topically-adjacent orchestrator notes?
gold: MiniLM pulls a tight cluster of topically-adjacent orchestrator notes into a 0.50-0.55 cosine band, so neither a raw cosine cut nor a top1-top2 margin cut separates a true positive from useless-but-topical matches. The discriminating signal is external-gap (fraction of the note's content tokens recurring in the task text): the one real positive measured externalGap 0.34 vs every topical negative <=0.17. The cosine floor was dropped from 0.55 to 0.50 because the only positive label (resolveOwner / note-mq7kyiir6sx) sat at top1=0.548, margin=0.017 and the old gate abstained and MISSED the win. Thresholds are calibrated on n=1 positive â€” provisional.
title: external-gap, not cosine/margin, is the load-bearing discriminator; cosine floor was lowered 0.55->0.50

question: What specific characteristic must a note have to pass the `requireEmpirical` and `projectLocality` guards, rather than being rejected as a general principle?
gold: requireEmpirical and the projectLocality guard mean a note must be concrete project-local scar-tissue (a gotcha, a decision-with-reason, a root cause) to be injected or to predict a user preference. General PRINCIPLES ('always prefer X', 'best practice') deliberately do NOT qualify â€” the base model already knows them, so injecting them is pure overhead. A vague topical note will never clear the gate, which is why KB authoring guidance insists notes be written empirically and project-locally.
title: Only EMPIRICAL project-local notes can fire the gates; general principles/best-practices are rejected by design

question: What condition must be met for `lib/ask-promote.js` to flip the live decider from the heuristic to the learned classifier?
gold: The hand-tuned heuristic is the live decider by default. A separately-trained logistic classifier (scripts/ask-clf-*) runs ALONGSIDE in shadow, writing shadow_decision/shadow_conf to .graph/ask-journal.jsonl as training signal WITHOUT deciding. lib/ask-promote.js runs a comparator each cycle and only flips .graph/ask-clf/mode.json from 'heuristic' to 'learned' (one-way, shadow->enforce) once the model beats the heuristic by a margin over a stable window. A missing model/mode file degrades to pure heuristic, so the gate stays usable offline. Same pattern mirrors edge-clf/mode.json.
title: Learned ask/edge classifiers run in SHADOW; live source flips heuristic->learned only via a one-way promotion

question: What specific costs did the benchmark identify as the reason orchestrator-ON arms performed worse than OFF on self-solvable tasks?
gold: The gates default to abstain because the benchmark found that on self-solvable tasks every orchestrator-ON arm did MORE work than OFF â€” injecting context the model didn't need is not free: it pays consult-overhead C (cache cost to hold the graph) AND nudges the model into extra deliberation. The whole point of the context-need gate is to suppress that tax by injecting only on a confident empirical match. This is why 'predict by default / inject only when confident' is a hard project stance, not mere caution.
title: Abstain-by-default exists to avoid the 'over-deliberation tax' measured in bench/report-v2..v7

question: What specific fields are captured in the frozen snapshot that `buildGraph` stores in `overlay.snapshots` when it first encounters a Claude native task?
gold: When buildGraph first sees a Claude native task it adopts a frozen snapshot ({subject, description, status, blockedBy, owner, metadata, snapshotted_at}) into overlay.snapshots; that snapshot â€” not the native .json file â€” is authoritative for structure. When the native file is later removed by the cleanupPeriodDays retention sweep, aggregateWorkspace falls back to the snapshot, so tasks don't vanish from the graph. Editing only the native file won't necessarily win.
title: Overlay snapshot is authoritative for task structure; the native file is a live echo

question: What value does `emitDiff` write to `status_changed` when a task's status override is present in the previous overlay but absent in the new one?
gold: emitDiff writes status_changed -> 'ready' for any task whose status override is ABSENT in the new overlay but present in prev (i.e. the override was deleted, e.g. on releaseClaim). On rehydrate the code explicitly skips node.status === 'ready' so the sentinel is never persisted back as a real status. Treating 'ready' as a stored status value will corrupt the diff logic.
title: status:'ready' is a SENTINEL in overlay sync meaning 'override cleared', not a real status

question: What condition must be true for a note to be re-pullable by the edge-judge, and what value is stamped on `judgedAtEpoch[key]` when a 'no edge' verdict is reached?
gold: overlay.epoch is a monotonic counter bumped on every note/task ADD. A note is re-pullable by the edge-judge only when judgedAtEpoch[key] < epoch; a 'no edge' verdict stamps judgedAtEpoch[key]=epoch so it stays out of the queue until the graph actually changes. judgeCursor persists the judge's queue position across daemon restarts so it never re-walks the whole graph. judgedClusters is the node-dedup analogue keyed by cluster signature.
title: Incremental edge-judge gates on epoch / judgedAtEpoch / judgeCursor â€” not on cosine alone

question: What is the `delaySeconds` value used for the idle heartbeat `ScheduleWakeup` when no loop is active?
gold: When no loop is active the system tells the agent to call loop_control({action:'start', tokenBudget:5000000, maxIterations:6250, minPoll:30, maxPoll:300, batch:4, maxConcurrency:6}). The idle heartbeat ScheduleWakeup uses delaySeconds=7200 (2h). These exact defaults govern autonomous-loop cost/cadence and can't be guessed off-repo.
title: Shipped default heartbeat loop controls: 5M token budget, 6250 iters, 30-300s poll, batch 4, conc 6; idle wakeup 7200s

question: What is the naming convention for the per-attempt frozen directories in `bench/heldout/frozen`, and where are their corresponding graders stored?
gold: bench/heldout/frozen holds frozen attempt dirs named like api-contract-off-0, claim-task-on-gated-0, bench-metric-on-search-1 â€” the suffix is the experiment arm (orchestrator off vs on, and the on-mode: gated/search/iterative) plus an index, paired with a per-challenge grader in bench/heldout/graders/<challenge>.grader.js. This is how the self-learn benchmark compares conditions; the naming is the contract.
title: Heldout bench fixtures encode A/B arms in the directory name: <challenge>-<off|on>-<gated|search|iterative>-<N>

question: What namespacing format must be used when referencing a task across sessions, and how does native-tasks.js key the unified workspace task list?
gold: Native Claude Code task IDs are local to a session; any cross-session/workspace reference must be the namespaced key `{session-uuid}/{id}`. native-tasks.js unions all session task files into one workspace list keyed this way (deps are intra-session blockedBy, namespaced to the same session).
title: Cross-session task IDs must be namespaced {session}/{id}

question: What is the specific file path layout that `native-tasks.js` wraps, and why is it intentionally the only file that reads it?
gold: The `~/.claude/tasks/{session}/{id}.json` layout (and the projects-dir encoding) is UNDOCUMENTED / internal to Claude Code. native-tasks.js is deliberately the single adapter for it â€” if a Claude Code version changes the format, only this file should need updating. Don't read those files anywhere else.
title: native-tasks.js is the SOLE adapter for the undocumented on-disk task layout

question: What specific command must be run to make a locally-trusted CA available so the daemon's /mcp endpoint can be served over HTTPS?
gold: A self-signed cert can't shortcut local HTTPS: TLS checks the issuer against the trust store regardless of locality, so `mkcert -install` (adds a locally-trusted CA) is mandatory to serve the daemon's /mcp over HTTPS. This is the only reason the setup wizard insists on mkcert over a hand-rolled cert.
title: mkcert is required because TLS validates the cert issuer, not localhost

question: What is the only surface that renders inline MCP Apps UI in the desktop app, and why do local stdio MCP servers not qualify?
gold: Shipped defaults: PORT=8787 (dashboard/graph), HTTPS_PORT=8788 (/mcp over locally-trusted HTTPS). The HTTPS custom-connector path is the ONLY surface that renders inline MCP Apps UI in the desktop app â€” local stdio MCP servers do not render it; otherwise you fall back to the preview panel.
title: Daemon ports: HTTP 8787, HTTPS 8788; inline UI only via custom connector

question: What happens to a Write/Edit/Bash-write operation when the orchestrator daemon is unreachable â€” is it allowed or blocked?
gold: orch-gate.js denies a Write/Edit/Bash-write ONLY on a definitive 'no claim for this session'; if the daemon is unreachable, or the hook itself throws, it allows the edit (fail-open by design â€” never brick edits). So the gate is a guardrail, not a hard security boundary against a down daemon.
title: The PreToolUse write-gate FAILS OPEN when the daemon is unreachable

question: What specific condition does the gate check to allow a write, and what does it fail to verify about the task's legitimacy?
gold: Once a task has a registered worktree, the gate denies writes outside that worktree path (use the path from branch_task). Honest limit: it checks for a claimed in_progress task + worktree existence, not status truth â€” a rubber-stamp claim still passes it.
title: Gate enforces writes happen INSIDE the registered worktree, but can't verify task legitimacy

question: What is the maximum number of initiatives the self-learn planner is allowed to output per run?
gold: Hard rules born from a real runaway: the planner NEVER cancels/supersedes/replans an in-flight task (that's the user's call), NEVER duplicates an open task (suggest_links + dedup BEFORE TaskCreate), caps output at 1-3 initiatives, and STOPs rather than fabricate busywork â€” graph bloat is failure.
title: The self-learn planner is ADDITIVE-ONLY â€” it caused a runaway once

question: What specific condition causes `decideOptimize` to return `'stuck'` rather than a silent stop reason like `'diminishing'` or `'budget'`?
gold: decideOptimize returns 'stuck' (â†’ request_guidance) when the last K rounds produced no real win (no winner, or guardrail regression). 'stuck' deliberately outranks the silent stop reasons (diminishing/budget) because a problem failing every round needs human judgement, not a quiet drop. The only human-in-loop path is escalate â€” NEVER auto-cancel/replan.
title: A stuck optimization ESCALATES to a human, never self-drops or auto-replans

question: What is the decision precedence order used by the optimize loop when determining whether to stop or continue iterating?
gold: DEFAULTS = { epsilon: 0.01, diminishing_rounds: 3 }; mis-set (negative/NaN) knobs fall back to defaults so a bad knob can't silently disable the control. Decision precedence (first match wins): target-converged â†’ stuck â†’ diminishing-converged â†’ budget â†’ iterate.
title: Optimize-loop defaults: epsilon=0.01, diminishing_rounds(K)=3, fixed precedence

question: What environment variable was added to override the `process.cwd()`-based workspace resolution in `mcp-graph.js`?
gold: mcp-graph.js used to post process.cwd() as the daemon workspace on startup, so any process loading the orchestrator MCP (e.g. a headless agent in a git worktree) hijacked the GLOBAL workspace pointer â€” repointing the live graph and blinding agents to the real workspace's learnings. Now honors ORCH_WORKSPACE when set (else cwd).
title: ORCH_WORKSPACE overrides cwd-as-workspace (dogfood-finding #1)

question: What does PLUMBING capture that causes it to under-count the true overhead, and what should NET be interpreted as as a result?
gold: MCP tool-schema tokens are cached into the system prompt and amortized across the session, NOT attributable per-message. So PLUMBING captures only tool_use/tool_result round-trips and under-counts the always-resident schema overhead. Read NET as an upper bound on work-only cost and PLUMBING as a lower bound on true orchestration overhead.
title: Bench PLUMBING under-counts the always-resident MCP schema tax

question: What is the corroboration guard condition that must be satisfied for a WIN verdict in the v4 benchmark?
gold: The v4 benchmark decomposes each arm into W (real work=diffTokens), H (hardness=outputâˆ’W), C (consult overhead=ONâˆ’OFF cache cost). A WIN needs all four guards: precondition H_offâ‰¥2Ã—W_off, fairness both-solveâ‰¥0.8, margin METRIC>0 and >pooled stdev, corroboration W_on/W_offâ‰¤1.1. Any guard failing â†’ NO-WIN.
title: Bench WIN requires all four guards to PASS; METRIC=(H_offâˆ’H_on)Ã—5 âˆ’ C

question: Where is a cross-workspace ghost edge stored, and how is the foreign node's status resolved?
gold: A dependency on a node in another workspace is a 'ghost edge': it lives in the consumer's overlay (fromWorkspace set means the provider lives elsewhere), and the foreign status is resolved on demand (cached, cycle-guarded) rather than stored. Don't look for it in the provider's graph.
title: Cross-workspace ghost edges store on the CONSUMER, foreign status resolved lazily

question: What status does a code task complete with under the autonomous orch-loop, and what action does the self-learn-judge explicitly NOT perform even after picking a winner?
gold: Under the autonomous orch-loop, every spawned code task works in an isolated orch/attempt/<slug> worktree, commits there, and completes as 'MERGE PENDING' â€” it never edits the live checkout and never merges to main. The self-learn-judge picks a winner but (in hold-merge mode) does NOT merge; merge is a deliberate human/dispatcher step.
title: Heartbeat-loop code work is hold-merge: completes as MERGE PENDING, never merges to main

question: What does the staleness sweep release, and what cache does it bust when reverting an agent's in_progress claim?
gold: Agent liveness fix #11: /agent/done releases the in_progress task the agent held; a staleness sweep releases abandoned claims (kill/crash/idle/cross-session) before reading native and busts the agg cache so reverted status shows same-build; releaseClaim also reverts native status to keep write-through in sync.
title: /agent/done CASCADES to release the task an agent held (fixes phantom in_progress)

question: What field must `taskTranscript` use to correlate a task's logical assignee with the harness agent record that carries `transcript_path`, given that the two never share a matching key?
gold: A task's recorded assignee is the LOGICAL worker name passed to start_task, but the agent record carrying transcript_path is registered by the SubagentStart hook under an opaque random harness agent_id, so the two never match by key. taskTranscript must correlate by session + claim-window time-overlap (harnessTranscriptForTask) instead of a direct lookup.
title: Task assignee is a logical name; transcript_path lives under a random harness agent_id

question: What condition causes `harnessTranscriptForTask` to return null rather than widening the window?
gold: In harnessTranscriptForTask a missing/unparsable lastChanged becomes Date.now() and an agent with no endedAt (still running) is treated as ending now, so the window widens rather than dropping the row; only a NaN firstSeen (winStart) returns null. Overlap >= 0 (intervals merely touching) counts as a match, and the largest overlap wins.
title: Transcript window-correlation widens, not rejects, on missing bounds

question: What specific note content causes a failure to be excluded from the `rejected[]` ledger in `digestRejected`?
gold: digestRejected's rejected[] = verdict losers (source:'verdict', carrying beatenBy=winner) plus GENUINE dead-end failures (source:'failure'). Failures whose note says superseded/duplicate/consolidated are deliberately excluded because they are replaced work, not dead ends â€” re-proposing them is fine.
title: rejected[] ledger excludes superseded/duplicate/consolidated failures

question: What condition must be met for the shared-session transcript hop to be allowed by `anySession: taskTokens`?
gold: taskTranscript resolves in order: assignee's own transcript_path -> per-session binding -> harness window-correlation -> the task's shared session transcript. The last (shared-session) hop is gated by anySession: taskTokens allows it ONLY when the session maps to a single task, while /costflow always allows it because splitSessionTokens divides the shared total honestly.
title: Session-transcript token fallback is gated so a shared total isn't painted across many tasks

question: What was the original rate limit for gated searches before it was raised, and why was it increased for bench trials?
gold: checkGatedRateLimit caps gated searches at 20 per rolling 60s window per IP. It was deliberately raised from 3 because all bench trial runs share the 127.0.0.1 bucket and a low limit caused spurious abstains between sequential trials.
title: Gated-search rate limit is 20 calls / 60s per IP (raised from 3 for bench trials)

question: What summary line format must each test file print before exiting, and what exit code does it use when there are failures?
gold: The ~150 files in test/ use no test framework. Each requires the target module directly (e.g. require('../daemon.js')), prints 'PASS <label>'/'FAIL <label>' lines, ends with 'N passed, M failed', and process.exit(fail===0?0:1). New tests must follow this shape rather than reaching for jest/mocha.
evidence: test/rejected-digest.test.js; 151 test/ files match the convention
title: Tests are plain Node with no framework: PASS/FAIL lines, 'N passed, M failed', exit nonzero

question: What percentage of rows in the economy-bench task-transcript grader registry have no transcript_path and no session, requiring attribution solely via byWindow overlap with the task's claim window?
gold: The task-transcript scenario grader (which the agent never sees) builds a registry where ~40% of rows have no transcript_path and no session â€” attributable ONLY by overlapping the task's claim window against byWindow. The prose spec describes only direct + session lookup, so a spec-faithful impl fails the edge cases; the ON arm's KB note is what seeds the window-overlap fallback. This is the intended OFF-vs-ON delta of the benchmark.
title: economy-bench task-transcript grader injects ~40% correlation-only rows a spec-faithful impl misses
